slides.heading: Bulgarian split squat
slides.body: Set up the exercise, then keep a useful training record.
slides.narration: Bulgarian Split Squat: Form, Setup and Common Fixes. This is a short guide to the setup and training record in the IZEM article. It uses equipment and text, rather than a movement demonstration. The full article links to the ACE and NASM exercise libraries for demonstrations.

slides.heading: Start with the setup
slides.body: Use suitable stable equipment. Review technique before adding weight.
slides.narration: Choose suitable, stable exercise support and review the movement before adding weight. The Bulgarian split squat is a demanding exercise. ACE classifies it as advanced. If you are new to lifting or unsure of your technique, work with a qualified fitness professional. Stop if the exercise causes pain.

slides.heading: Record the equipment
slides.narration: The setup note records the support you actually used, the variation and the exact load. A note that says ten kilograms leaves room for confusion. Two ten kilogram dumbbells makes the load clear. Give a bodyweight, goblet or two dumbbell variation its own name in the log.

slides.heading: Write down both sides
slides.body: Label the leg on the floor as the working leg.
slides.narration: Label the side by the leg on the floor. Write left working leg and right working leg. Record what each side completed, rather than treating the target number as the result. If one side stops earlier, keep that difference in the note.

slides.heading: Count paired sets clearly
slides.body: Example: 2 sets × 8 reps per leg = 32 repetitions across both legs.
slides.narration: Here is a logging example, not a recommended workload. Suppose an existing program calls for two sets of eight repetitions per leg. Paired set one records eight left and eight right. Paired set two does the same. That is two sets for each leg, and thirty two repetitions across both legs. Also record the rest you actually took.

slides.heading: Keep the observation specific
slides.body: Note setup changes and what interrupted a set.
slides.narration: Write down any setup change or interruption. Balance loss and an awkward support position are useful observations to bring to a technique check. The tool cannot judge form or explain the cause of pain. It only formats what you enter, so your next session has a clearer record to start from.

slides.heading: Keep your note
slides.body: Copy the text. Entries are not saved by the page.
slides.narration: The note builder runs in the browser and does not send or save your entries. Copy the text into your own training notes before leaving or reloading the page. For the full instructions, source notes and logging example, read the Bulgarian split squat guide at youraicoach dot life. The free workout planner is a separate next step for planning the rest of the session.
